instruction: I have hearing difficulties and can't hear system sounds. Can you enable visual alerts so the screen flashes when there's a notification?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: VISUAL_BELL=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences visual-bell 2>/dev/null | grep -c true); if [ "$VISUAL_BELL" -gt 0 ]; then echo "Visual bell enabled"; else echo "Visual bell not enabled"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling visual bell via Settings > Accessibility > Visual Alerts. Evaluator checks visual-bell setting. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences visual-bell setting, which is the appropriate GNOME setting for visual alerts/screen flashing
Command logic is robust: uses timeout, handles errors with 2>/dev/null, and outputs clear success/failure messages
check_include_exclude metric correctly verifies the command output contains 'Visual bell enabled' and doesn't contain error indicators
Data flow is correct: vm_command_line getter executes command and returns stdout, metric validates output matches expected patterns
Complete coverage: instruction requires enabling visual alerts, evaluator checks the exact system setting that controls this feature
No postconfig needed: gsettings values can be read at any time after modification
